items.text: Andy Burnham, the UK Prime Minister, stated that the Islamic Republic is responsible for the attack on the Ferford base. The UK summoned the Iranian ambassador and imposed new sanctions on Tehran. The attack was definitely directed by the Revolutionary Guards.

The spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition announced that the country's air defense successfully intercepted and destroyed incoming missiles from Yemen. Minutes after an air threat warning, several explosions occurred in Riyadh, likely due to the interceptor missiles. The Saudi Civil Defense announced about 10 minutes later that the threat had been neutralized.

The interrogation session of 12 citizens related to the Qaleh Chenan case was held at the second interrogation branch of Karun County. Charges include moharebeh, baghi, disruption of public order, and conspiracy against national security. The accused are denied access to lawyers and meetings with their families.

At least six protests were held today, Monday, October 12, by retired telecommunications workers in Ahvaz, Kermanshah, Sanandaj, Isfahan, Khorramabad, and laid-off workers of Khavar spinning factory in Rasht. Their demands included unpaid wages and benefits, healthcare services, and job status clarification. These protests were reported in at least six locations.

The Israeli army announced the discovery and destruction of an underground tunnel network hundreds of meters long in southern Lebanon. Weapons such as Kalashnikovs, machine guns, and anti-tank missiles were found in these tunnels. The Israeli army stated it will not allow Hezbollah to harm Israeli civilians or soldiers.

Alireza Beiranvand attended the match between Nirooye Zamini Tehran and Karagostar after being dismissed from Tractor. The coach of Nirooye Zamini stated that Beiranvand's status with the team is still unclear. Tasnim News Agency reported that Beiranvand must begin his military service on November 1, 2026, and his medical requests were denied.

Esteghlal football team won 2-1 against Al-Gharafa Qatar in their second match of the Asian Elite League. Goals for Esteghlal were scored by Yaser Asani and Hossein Goodarzi. The victory was marked by Asani's superb goal and Habib Farabbasi's consecutive saves.

The match between Al-Nassr Saudi Arabia and Neftchi Uzbekistan in the Asian Champions League was delayed by one hour due to a security alert about a missile threat. Saudi authorities intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards Riyadh. After the security was confirmed, players returned to the field and the game continued.

Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have intensified. Saudi Arabia and the legitimate Yemeni government forces have launched heavy attacks on Houthi positions. Saudi Arabia has threatened a serious response, supported by Western allies including the UK.

Jaber Rajabi said that the mindset of part of the power in the Islamic Republic is based on an "all or nothing" logic and tries to ensure the regime's survival by holding regional security and economy hostage. He added that the Islamic Republic is expanding crises across the region to force others to make concessions. Rajabi also mentioned that regional countries might find short-term confrontation costs with the Islamic Republic less burdensome than enduring long-term threats.

The audio version 24 with Fardad Farahzad discusses the confrontation between Britain and the Islamic Republic. The involvement of the IRGC in a security plot has also been discovered. This topic was raised in the program.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh expressed happiness after Esteghlal's victory over Al-Gharafa in the Asian Elite League, emphasizing the team's effort and defense. He praised the players' performance and noted the challenges posed by bad weather and injuries to two players. Despite difficulties, he highlighted the team's unity and pride.

1,700 Iranian activists and families of victims supported awarding the 2026 Freedom Prize of the Friedrich Naumann Foundation to Reza Pahlavi. This support was announced in a letter prepared by the Patriotic Iranian Doctors group. The letter was delivered to the Friedrich Naumann Foundation.

Mukhtar Alboshoka, an Ahwazi Arab political prisoner, is in critical condition on the eighth day of his hunger strike. He has been transferred to Arak prison and has not yet been returned to Sheiban prison. The Karun Human Rights Organization has warned about the risk to his life.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, described the January massacre as the largest street killing in Iran's history. He stated that this massacre extended to hospital assaults and continued repression in prisons with increased executions. The families of the disappeared also continue to face harassment by the Islamic Republic.

Bloomberg reported that with increased attacks by the Islamic Republic around the Strait of Hormuz, at least 10 supertankers and several Suezmax tankers have changed course or stopped. This situation could disrupt oil transfer near Fujairah and regional exports. The reduction in receiving tankers may slow down the oil transfer process.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, spoke about the major crime in Dey month, highlighting that some young couples lost one partner at the start of their married life. These stories are among the most painful narratives about the destruction of their dreams. The survivors of the martyrs face this harsh reality.

The Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran announced that drones of the Islamic Republic targeted the Azadi camp in Kuyeh on Monday noon. The attack caused no casualties but resulted in material damage. The reports were published by Rudaw network.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that the families of the martyrs want to achieve the goal of overthrowing the Islamic Republic. He added that these individuals were the best children of Iran who sacrificed their lives for freedom. He also noted that they loved life.

Ivar Farhadi stated that the incident at the Fairford base should not be seen merely as a security event in the UK because the base is used by American forces. The UK Prime Minister's announcement of the IRGC's role and support from foreign ministers could lead to increased sanctions and joint counterterrorism cooperation. These actions will increase international pressure on the Islamic Republic.

The UK court reviewed Mustafa Sepahvand's messages and audio files related to promises of money and resolving his legal case in Iran. Sepahvand and two other defendants have denied their charges. The prosecution claims they monitored Iran International journalists.

Gina Romero, the UN special rapporteur, started a 24-hour hunger strike. She announced this action in solidarity with the people of Iran and joining the campaign of Tuesdays against executions. Romero called for a halt to executions and independent monitoring of prisoners.

Ahmad Vahidi, the commander of the IRGC, stated that no extra-regional power has the right to intervene in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf. He expressed this position on the social network X. Vahidi rejected hegemonic presence and threats in these areas.

Qatar Airways announced the temporary suspension of its flights to Riyadh and Dammam. This decision was made following recent developments in Saudi Arabia and in coordination with relevant authorities. Qatar Airways has asked passengers to check the company's website or app for flight status updates.

Amir Giti said that the Islamic Republic, amid tensions with the US, is using one of its last regional levers by intensifying Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He added that if a coalition led by Saudi Arabia directly confronts the Houthis, the Islamic Republic will have to choose between supporting the Houthis and avoiding conflict with its neighbors. He also mentioned that threats like cutting communication cables under the Persian Gulf impose costs ultimately borne by the Iranian people.

The Wall Street Journal reported that internet-connected surveillance cameras can be used with AI to monitor military movements and assist attacks. Mehdi Saremi-Far said these cameras played a role similar to pagers in Israeli attacks on Hezbollah during attacks on the Islamic Republic by Israel and the US. He also added that limiting internet access can increase infrastructure vulnerability and does not necessarily prevent cyber operations.

The General Authority of Civil Aviation of Saudi Arabia announced the extension of the suspension of activities at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The suspension is necessary to complete safety inspections and ensure the operational readiness of the airport facilities. The date for resuming activities has not been announced.

The Hengaw human rights organization reported that the death sentence of Ayoub Mohammad Nabil, a 28-year-old Iraqi citizen, was secretly carried out in Lakan prison in Rasht. He had previously been sentenced to death on charges of spying for Saudi-backed proxy groups. Mohammad Nabil denied the charges and faced torture during detention.

Mohammadreza Zanouzi, owner of Tractor club, criticized the inequality in team flights to competitions, stating one team flew to Qatar with a government VIP flight while his team faced travel difficulties. He also mentioned player fatigue and the draw with Al-Shamal Qatar. Zanouzi commented on Alireza Beiranvand's future, emphasizing the importance of keeping young players.

Russian experts report that Saudi Arabia may intensify bombing in Yemen, but military victory over the Houthis will be difficult. Saudi Arabia is trying to encourage the US to participate directly in military operations, but the US is trying to prevent this scenario. Negotiation with the Houthis is easier than military defeat.

Hackers increased the temperature of refrigerators and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets in France to 50 degrees Celsius, causing food spoilage and multi-million euro damages. The Paris prosecutor's office announced that internet-connected refrigerators of several major companies were targeted, and the French Prime Minister ordered an investigation. Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany, and Belgium were also affected by similar attacks.

Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia stopped issuing public warnings about imminent attacks days before deadly attacks on Riyadh airport. The Saudi government has not explained the reason for stopping these warnings. This situation has raised questions about Riyadh's ability to protect its citizens.

OPEC and non-OPEC ministers announced unprecedented increases in maritime transport and insurance costs. They emphasized the importance of protecting international shipping routes. These cost increases have intensified economic and inflationary pressures.

Donald Trump stated that the Islamic Republic of Iran currently lacks a clear leader and senior officials, causing difficulties for the US in identifying negotiation counterparts. He said no one wants to be president of Iran and Washington does not know who to negotiate with. Trump also mentioned that the US may have overreacted in dealing with Iranian leaders.

Mohammed al-Bukhaiti from the Houthis warned that if the US intervenes in the aggression against Yemen, it will face a swift and painful response. He also warned workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports that these locations have become legitimate targets. These statements were made in an interview with Agence France-Presse.

Donald Trump denied opponents' claims about China and Russia helping the Islamic Republic. He said if such help exists, it is very limited and he does not believe it happens at all. Trump added that if such actions were taken, the US would have quickly known about it.

Donald Trump, the US President, said that the Islamic Republic now has no leader or senior officials. He added that Washington is facing difficulty identifying a negotiating partner in Iran. Trump also said that perhaps they overdid it in dealing with Iran's leaders.

Kim Jong Un visited North Korea's new defense industry museum, where the intercontinental ballistic missile Hwasong-20 is displayed. The museum also features drones and weapons developed during his leadership. North Korea also announced a tactical ballistic missile test and fired several missiles toward eastern waters.

Donald Trump said Iranian officials want an agreement but do not know how to achieve it. Saadollah Zarei warned about increasing conflicts and the possibility of military confrontation if negotiations fail. These statements were published by Iran International.

Ahmad Batabi identified three main vulnerabilities of the Islamic Republic's security system: weak hardware and software, lack of equipment updates, and human infiltration. He also stated that Israel's access to advanced cybersecurity and artificial intelligence technologies has created a significant difference in capabilities between the two sides.

Deutsche Welle reported, citing two senior defected members of special forces and the Ministry of Intelligence, that kidnapping and assassination operations against opponents inside and outside Iran were planned in a secret place called 'Dakhmeh'. This report was published by Ali Hassanpour, a journalist from Iran International.

Kamyar Behrang says the dispute between Masoud Pezeshkian and Saeed Jalili over negotiations is part of an internal conflict within the Islamic Republic to determine Ali Khamenei's legacy. Both factions try to attribute responsibility for Khamenei's policies to him while absolving themselves of the consequences. The people of Iran bear the cost of this conflict through shrinking livelihoods.

Aydin Panahi stated that this winter, the Islamic Republic will face greater gas shortages and fuel supply limitations for power plants. Reduced gas injection into old oil fields may decrease Iran's oil production capacity. This situation will lead to increased air pollution and more pressure on people and industries.

Sadegh Beigdelie says that the continuation of the siege and the possibility of reimposing sanctions are tools used by the Trump administration to force the Islamic Republic to accept an agreement. He believes the factions' disagreement is about how the agreement is structured and the share of power and economic resources afterward. The principle of negotiation itself is not disputed.

Shahram Khaledi says Houthi attacks and increased security pressures may change Saudi Arabia's calculations. He mentioned the possibility of military cooperation between Saudi Arabia and Israel against the Houthis. The Israeli Air Force might also participate in future attacks.

Rasoul Bakhshi Dastjerdi stated that seventy percent of liquidity is held by a few people and money is not in the right place. He added that the Central Bank encourages speculation by selling dollars and gold to people. He also emphasized that public participation should lead to involvement of all people in production and use of cooperatives' capacity.

Rasul Sanai Rad, deputy of Khamenei's ideological-political office, wrote in Javan newspaper that no US warship has the courage to enter the Strait of Hormuz, and US ground forces lack the capability to take action on Iranian coasts. He added that the Islamic Republic has complete intelligence and military dominance over the strait and is capable of closing it.

Naser Atabati, head of Tehran's judiciary, stated that the judiciary must confront any behavior promoting nudity and immorality. He emphasized that the current situation in some cases goes beyond unveiling and requires serious measures. He also noted that many people oppose nudity in public places.

Cristiano Ronaldo kissed the Saudi national emblem on his jersey during the Al-Nassr match against Neftchi Uzbekistan. After the game, he held a scarf with Saudi symbols and saluted the fans. This gesture received widespread attention on social media and among Saudis.

Shahram Jamali, who is serving his sentence in Amol prison, was granted a one-week leave starting Sunday, October 11. The leave was approved with the provision of a pay slip. This news was reported by HRANA news agency.

People in Meymeh, Isfahan province, protested against the new name of their county. The protest took place on Sunday, October 11, and turned violent after an attack by authorities. Several protesters were injured in the incident.

Foreign ministers of 32 countries led by the UK condemned cyberattacks, sabotage, and violent actions attributed to the Islamic Republic abroad. They supported London's assessment of the IRGC's role in a possible bombing plot at the Ferford base. This news was reported by Alireza Mohibi.

Morteza Kazemian says Trump's remarks about targeting leaders of the Islamic Republic are threats and humiliation, indicating Washington seeks a diplomatic agreement with Tehran. The Islamic Republic is simultaneously strengthening its military and security capabilities. These measures aim to counter internal protests and prevent widespread social uprisings.

Ruhollah Rahimpour says Israel is inclined to participate in the war against the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic. The goal is to reduce missile attack threats against Israel and prevent disruption in Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb Strait shipping. This route is strategically important for Israel's economic security.

Amir Ghalenoei explained the status of the national football team and the football federation board meeting in a televised interview. He criticized the lack of questions from board members and denied promising a championship. Ghalenoei also stated that he adheres to disciplinary and technical principles regarding the exclusion of Mehdi Qaedi from the national team.

The European Union has sanctioned nearly 1,600 companies and managers in the Russian military industry. Kaja Kallas, the EU's foreign policy chief, emphasized the need to increase pressure on Moscow. These sanctions are part of the EU's new measures.
Yeganeh Hosseinzayi, a 16-year-old child marriage victim, was killed by her husband in Bakharz county. The suspect has been arrested by the police. This incident occurred in Khorasan Razavi province.
The execution sentence of a prisoner convicted of killing a traffic police officer was carried out in Minab prison. The sentence had been previously issued. The execution took place in Minab prison.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, stated that during the ongoing war, they sometimes have to reduce internet speed. This measure is due to the importance of databases and internet-based services. The reduction in internet speed is to protect the country's assets.

Ahmad Bakhshayesh Ardestani stated that the regime's structure will not collapse solely due to military attacks and serious change occurs only if people take to the streets. He mentioned the possibility of top commanders being killed in new US attacks. He also said that if a bomb explodes in Iran, a retaliatory strike on the Dimona facilities in Israel is possible.

Security measures have intensified in Mimeh, Isfahan following protests against the renaming of the county. During the crackdown on protests on October 11, several protesters were injured and arrested. Authorities also detained some of the injured in hospitals.

The death sentence of Amirhossein Akbari Monfared, a political prisoner in Evin Prison, was confirmed by Branch 41 of the Supreme Court. The sentence was communicated to him on October 11, 2026. He was sentenced to death for rebellion through membership in the Mojahedin-e Khalq Organization.

The human rights website Halvash reported a clash between the Revolutionary Guards and armed individuals in the Taftan heights. About 40 backup vehicles of the Revolutionary Guards were dispatched to the area. This news was reported by sources from the Halvash website.

A birthday ceremony for Reza Eskandarpour was held at his gravesite. Attendees chanted "Hope for freedom" during the event. Reza Eskandarpour, aged 37, was killed on January 8, 2026, while helping the wounded in Aryashahr, Tehran.
A citizen in Sarakhs was arrested by intelligence officers for sending videos and images to foreign media.
Messages received by Iran International indicate rising food prices and business recession. Unemployment insurance payments are also not being made. This issue was reported by Leila Saadati.

Esteghlal club criticized the coverage of their victory against Al-Gharafa on Iranian state TV, calling it unfair and unprofessional. The club expressed dissatisfaction with the focus on issues like Yaser Asani's contract and the direct flight to Qatar instead of the victory itself. They warned that if this approach continues, they will reconsider their media interactions with the state broadcaster.

Reza Sepahvand, spokesperson for the Energy Commission of the Parliament, stated that the US has intervened in the cryptocurrencies of the Islamic Republic and seized some amounts. He called the seizure theft and said the seized resources belonged to individuals, institutions, and the government. He also explained that the names of trusts are not disclosed to bypass sanctions and economic blockade.

A retiree reported issues with supplementary insurance coverage. Basij forces are fully covered and present in the streets of Mashhad, setting up checkpoints. In Karaj, there are disputes about the amount of ration cards and the salaries of county employees.

Student protests in France continue into the fourth week, demanding more teachers and better educational conditions. Iranian officials have responded to the protests by comparing internet conditions in Iran and France. A full report is provided by Sajedeh Sharifi.

Borussia Dortmund officially extended Niko Kovac's contract until June 2029. Kovac has been coaching the team since January 2025 and holds the best record among the club's Bundesliga coaches. Dortmund finished as Bundesliga runners-up last season and is currently in second place this season.

Unemployment insurance payments by Social Security have been significantly delayed. People complain about non-payment and the resulting financial difficulties. Banks and Social Security are unresponsive, and some branches have promised future payments.

A group of retired telecommunications workers in Tehran gathered on Monday, October 12, to protest their livelihood problems in front of the Yeganeh telecommunications complex. They chanted the slogan "Don't say we don't have it anymore, we are tired of this slogan." The protest highlights the retirees' livelihood issues.

Benjamin Netanyahu is trying, with US mediation, to gain Saudi Arabia's approval for Israel's participation in military operations against the Houthis in Yemen. This was reported by Haaretz newspaper. More details are provided in an interview with Babak Es-haqi.

Michael Jordan's signed jersey from the Last Dance season was sold for $14 million, breaking the record for the most expensive basketball memorabilia. Jordan wore this jersey in the second game of the 1998 NBA Finals. The purchase was made by Ron Fairman in a private deal.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh reacted to the Wall Street Journal report about the Islamic Republic's intention to expand the war if the US attacks again. He said if another attack occurs and developments proceed slowly like the 40-day war, the Islamic Republic will have the opportunity to recover its strength. It can also implement various plans and scenarios.

Israel's elections will be held in about two weeks. Benjamin Netanyahu will enter a competition that will determine his political future. The key question is whether Netanyahu can remain prime minister.

In the second week of the Asian Elite League, Esteghlal achieved its second consecutive victory and Tractor drew. Esteghlal club referred to people's livelihood problems and criticized the state TV's coverage of their victory against Al-Gharafa. Esteghlal considered focusing on marginal issues as biased.

The mother of Mohsen Ghahremanpour joined the campaign "9 apples, 9 months of separation." On the ninth month after her son's death, she placed 9 apples next to his pictures. Mohsen Ghahremanpour was shot by officers in Tehranpars on January 8, 2026, and died a week later.

Friedrich Merz, the German Chancellor, warned the Islamic Republic officials and Houthis to end destabilizing actions in the region. He called for Tehran to return to the negotiating table and to permanently open the Strait of Hormuz. He also emphasized that Iran must stop its military nuclear program.

Rwanda has signed a 10-year contract to host Formula One races called the Grand Prix of Africa starting in early 2030. The event will take place at the new Bugesera circuit near Kigali. The Formula One president called the deal historic, and Rwanda's president said it will boost economic development and tourism.

The head of Britain's internal intelligence agency stated that the Islamic Republic has increased its efforts this year to target more sensitive sites, including military facilities. He referred to a possible plot against the RAF Fairford airbase and said it was not the only case. The British Prime Minister also suggested Tehran's likely involvement in this plot.

The Iranian judiciary announced the execution of a person accused of running over and killing a police officer in Minab Jask. The death sentence was confirmed by the Supreme Court after an appeal. This execution is the 621st recorded execution in Iran since the beginning of 2026.

Nigel Farage announced that if his party wins the upcoming election, asylum application processing will be suspended for five years. About 90,000 pending cases will be canceled and new applications will be rejected. Returning refugees to origin or safe third countries and imposing sanctions if countries refuse to accept them were also mentioned.

The head of the judiciary in Isfahan province announced that Amir Salar Davoodi, a lawyer, was arrested for releasing an audio file of the marriage of Alireza Sepahi and Mahshad Keshani. The audio file was described as false by the judiciary head. Davoodi is accused of publishing content that caused public disturbance.

The Wall Street Journal, citing informed sources, reported that some Iranian officials have mentioned the possibility of a ground attack on neighboring countries if US attacks resume. This was discussed in talks with regional officials. No further details were provided.

Amnesty International stated that the Islamic Republic uses executions as a tool to intimidate people. The organization referred to the execution of five protesters in December 1404. It also emphasized that some of these individuals were tortured and denied access to a lawyer.

The head of the Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution announced a 5% quota for war-affected university entrance exam candidates. This quota applies to candidates whose homes were destroyed in the 12-day and 40-day wars and require major repairs. The resolution was approved on July 13, 2026, and has been announced for implementation.

Donald Trump stated that the US midterm elections will not affect his approach to the war with the Islamic Republic. Maryam Rahmati, a reporter from Iran International, reports on the latest war developments in Iran and the assessment of American officials. The report also covers the outlook for the continuation of the war.

Two Baloch human rights media reported the killing of several Fatimiyoun forces in clashes with armed individuals in the Chah Ahmad area of Taftan county. The clashes lasted more than seven hours, and military forces targeted the area with mortars and drones. Media affiliated with the IRGC also reported the killing of armed individuals, but exact casualty numbers remain unconfirmed.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, announced that 40 million people are eligible for a 500,000 toman increase in electronic ration credit. These include low-income individuals and households supported by welfare organizations. Meanwhile, reports of disruptions in the household registration process have emerged.

Media close to the IRGC reported the end of armed clashes in Sistan and Baluchestan. However, the Halvash website reported that the armed clash in the Taftan heights continues after seven hours. More details were provided in an interview with Mehdi Nakhl Ahmadi.

The Central Bank of Iran announced that some banking services to five cryptocurrency exchanges will be suspended for three days. This decision has caused widespread protests among users. Users report difficulties accessing their digital assets.

The Guardian reported increased concerns about the security of the Asian Cup following missile attacks by the Houthis on Riyadh. These attacks caused dozens of casualties and have made Asian football stars hesitant about traveling to Saudi Arabia. Five of the eight stadiums hosting the tournament are in Riyadh, where key matches will take place.

Kaja Kallas, the EU foreign policy chief, stated that the UK believes the IRGC is likely behind the threat against RAF Fairford. The EU has listed the IRGC as a terrorist organization and imposed sanctions on Iranian officials. Kallas emphasized the EU's strong support for the UK.

Hojatollah Abdolmaleki, the labor minister of Ebrahim Raisi's government, made statements about Iran's economic problems. These statements received widespread reactions on social media, with humorous and critical responses from the public. Adel Borang from Iran International reported on this issue.

Yahya Sari, the military spokesperson for the Houthis, stated that Saudi Arabia's Aramco oil facilities are legitimate targets for the group. He urged employees and citizens to stay away from these facilities and evacuate areas around Aramco, King Khalid Airport, and Riyadh refinery if Saudi Arabia attacks. Previous warnings about airports and airspace were also reiterated.

Following the announcement of the IRGC's role in the attack plan on the Ferford base, the head of Britain's internal intelligence said the Islamic Republic seeks to target important security centers, including military bases in Britain and other countries. These statements came amid widespread condemnation by countries. More details were provided in an interview with Tajeddin Soroush.

The Secretary-General of the Gulf Cooperation Council described the attacks by the Houthis supported by the Islamic Republic on Saudi Arabia as terrorist and savage acts. He stated these attacks indicate the Houthis' insistence on committing crimes. He also emphasized that Saudi Arabia's security is an integral part of the security of GCC member countries.

Foreign ministers of 32 countries issued a joint statement condemning security activities attributed to the Islamic Republic. Nordic media widely covered the statement, highlighting nuclear concerns and security threats. Swedish and Norwegian media focused on government reactions and warnings about the Islamic Republic's proxy networks in Europe.

Ali Amirian, silver medalist in the 800 meters at the Nagoya Asian Games, spoke about the difficulties in his early sports years. He ran from his village to the city for training and worked to cover expenses. Amirian mentioned coaching challenges and injuries and called for more support for athletics.

The chain stores of Intermarché in France were targeted by a cyberattack. The temperature of cooling equipment rose to 80 degrees Celsius, ruining fresh and frozen products. The store manager apologized to customers and announced that the products must be discarded.

Masoud Kanaani criticized industries for neglecting the employment of local forces in Khuzestan. He said the lack of job opportunities has caused some families to depend on the Relief Committee and Welfare Organization. Economic problems have also led to some students dropping out of school and university.

The 41st birthday ceremony of Aref Barati was held at his grave with the presence of his family and close ones. His sister said that his ideals have not been extinguished. Aref Barati was killed on January 8, 2026, during protests in Kuhchenar, Fars province.

The Iranian Navy announced that a tanker which had turned off its tracking systems and was damaged and caught fire in the restricted area east of the Strait of Hormuz was identified. The Navy monitors vessel movements continuously with deployed operational units. Vessels are also urged to comply with international laws and coordinate for safe passage.

Youssef Reji, Lebanon's foreign minister, announced his country's opposition to Iran's interference in Lebanon's internal affairs. He condemned Iran's attacks on Arab countries and stated that Hezbollah has dragged Lebanon into a futile war. The Lebanese government prioritized liberating occupied territories and regaining exclusive decision-making authority over war and peace.
Sepahan football team defeated Zob Ahan 2-1 in the Isfahan derby. With this victory, Sepahan reached 16 points and ranked fourth in the standings. Zob Ahan remained in fourteenth place with 7 points.

Today, on 21 Mehr, victims of the Etemad Iranian Credit Cooperative and Fajr Bahman Company gathered in front of Mashhad court. They demanded the resolution of financial cases and the return of their assets. The protesters also called for speeding up the case review process.

A citizen criticized the high prices of medicines in Iran in a video sent to Iran International. He said that the Islamic Republic officials do not care about people's medicine costs. The video reflects concerns about the medicine situation.
